This former army chief seized power in a 2014 coup, installed a military junta, and went on to serve as Thailand's prime minister for nearly a decade. Who is he?
Prayut Chan-o-cha: Prime Minister of Thailand from 2014 to 2023.

Serving as India's president from 2017 to 2022, he was the first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the Bharatiya Janata Party to hold that office, after serving as Governor of Bihar — who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind: President of India from 2017 to 2022.

Fought from 1921 to 1926, this conflict pitted Spain and later France against Berber guerrillas led by Abd el-Krim in northern Morocco, and saw history's first amphibious landing to use tanks and aircraft — which conflict?
Rif War: 1921–1926 war between Spain and Riffian tribes of Morocco.
Founded by a Varangian prince who settled at Novgorod in 862, this noble lineage ruled Kievan Rus' and, through its Moscow branch, the tsars of Russia until 1598 — what dynasty was it?
Rurikids: Noble lineage and rulers of Kievan Rus'. The Rurikids were the ruling dynasty of Kievan Rus' and its principalities following its disintegration.
Once expected to succeed his mother as India's prime minister, this politician died in a plane crash, clearing the way for his brother Rajiv to inherit the family's political mantle — who was he?
Serving as his country's foreign minister since 2004 — longer than anyone since the Soviet era — this diplomat also speaks fluent Sinhala and Dhivehi from his early postings — who is he?
This legendary Germanic hero slew the dragon Fafnir and was later murdered after a quarrel involving his wife and another woman he had unknowingly helped deceive — who is he?
The only prime minister to date from the modern Conservative Party of Canada, this Calgary economist co-founded the party and led the country from 2006 to 2015 — who is he?
Stephen Harper: Prime Minister of Canada from 2006 to 2015. Stephen Joseph Harper (born April 30, 1959) is a Canadian politician who served as the 22nd prime minister of Canada from 2006 to 2015.
A former brigadier-general who rose to Speaker of Singapore's Parliament, this politician resigned in 2023 after admitting to a years-long affair with a fellow MP — who is he?
Tan Chuan-Jin: Singaporean politician. Tan Chuan-Jin (born 10 January 1969) is a Singaporean former politician and brigadier-general.
At just 33, this Marxist revolutionary became president after a coup staged on his behalf, then launched sweeping reforms he called the people's democratic revolution — who is he?
Thomas Sankara: President of Burkina Faso from 1983 to 1987.
This Norse god sacrificed his right hand to bind the monstrous wolf Fenrir, and English weekdays still preserve his name in the middle of the work week — who is he?

Facing extradition from the UK to India over financial crimes, this businessman built his fortune as chairman of the country's largest spirits company and a sprawling conglomerate spanning aviation and real estate — who is he?
Vijay Mallya: Indian businessman and politician (born 1955)
Fought from 1879 to 1884 over nitrate-rich Atacama Desert territory, this conflict pitted Chile against an alliance of Bolivia and Peru, ending in a decisive Chilean victory — which conflict?
War of the Pacific: Territorial conflict between Chile and allied Peru and Bolivia (1879–84)

Despite a huge edge in tanks and aircraft, the Soviet Union took heavy losses and was expelled from the League of Nations after its November 1939 invasion of Finland — what was this three-and-a-half-month conflict called?
Winter War: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland.
A former steel-plant foundryman, this Soviet pilot orbited Earth once in 108 minutes aboard Vostok 1 and became an overnight global celebrity — who is he?
Which of these people was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Ryōkichi Yatabe (born 1851) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Jabir ibn Hayyan is an astronomer. The c. 215 treatises that survive today mainly deal with alchemy and chemistry, magic, and Shi'ite religious philosophy.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
What is the atomic number of Rhodium?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the atomic number of Argon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
In what year was Carlos Slim born?
Carlos Slim Helú (Spanish: [ˈkaɾlos esˈlin eˈlu, - esˈlim -]; born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.
In what year was Antoine Lavoisier born?
Antoine Lavoisier: It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
In what year was Travis Kalanick born?
Travis Kalanick: Travis Cordell Kalanick (born August 6, 1976) is an American businessman best known as the co-founder and former chief executive officer (CEO) of Uber.
In what year did Zhuge Liang die?
Zhuge Liang: After helping found Shu Han, Zhuge Liang exercised near-total authority over both civil and military affairs.
In what year did Marie Curie die?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
In which country is British Aerospace 146?
British Aerospace 146: United Kingdom. Production figures include the Avro RJ, an improved version from Avro International Aerospace, a subsidiary of BAE Systems.
Who is credited with discovering Fructose?
Fructose: Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut. Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a common monosaccharide, i.e. a simple sugar.
Who is credited with discovering LSD?
LSD: Albert Hofmann. LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
Who is credited with discovering Manganese?
Manganese: Johan Gottlieb Gahn. Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.

This mosquito species, native to tropical Southeast Asia and marked with distinctive white bands on its legs and body, has spread worldwide via international trade and travel, becoming a significant public health concern — what species is it?

Aedes albopictus (synonym Stegomyia albopicta), from the mosquito (Culicidae) family, also known as the (Asian) tiger mosquito or forest mosquito, is a species of mosquito native to the tropical and subtropical areas of Southeast Asia.
This parasitic intestinal illness, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, can produce cysts that survive for weeks in soil or nearly an hour under fingernails — what is it called?
Amoebiasis is an infection of the intestines caused by a parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Originally built by Hawker Siddeley and still produced under license in India today, this subsonic British trainer aircraft equips the Red Arrows aerobatic team — which jet?
BAE Systems Hawk is a British single-engine, subsonic, jet-powered advanced trainer aircraft.

This scientific discipline, a hybrid of chemistry and biology, studies the chemical processes occurring within living organisms and is generally divided into structural biology, enzymology, and metabolism — what's the field called?
Biochemistry (distinct from chemical biology), is the study of chemical processes within and relating to living organisms.

Named for its bread-like texture and potato-like flavor when cooked, this tropical tree fruit spread through Oceania via ancient seafaring migrations before European navigators brought Polynesian varieties to the Caribbean — which fruit?
Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a species of flowering tree in the mulberry and jackfruit family (Moraceae).
Wolves, domestic dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals all belong to this taxonomic genus, whose members are known for massive skulls, long legs, and short ears and tails. Name the genus?
Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
Which American political scientist drew fierce controversy as co-author of the 1994 book 'The Bell Curve' and author of the welfare-system critique 'Losing Ground'?
Charles Murray (political scientist) (born January 8, 1943) is an American political scientist.
Almost instantly after a vessel is injured, platelets swarm and fibrin cross-links to turn blood from liquid to gel, stopping the leak so repair can begin. What's the name for this clotting process?
Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on the region, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere — what is it?
Cougar (Puma concolor), also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large feline native to the Americas.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
A German-born British economist, he championed human-scale, appropriate technology in a hugely influential 1973 book ranked among the 100 most important since WWII — who is he?

E. F. Schumacher (16 August 1911 - 4 September 1977) was a German-born British statistician and economist who is best known for his proposals for human-scale, decentralised and appropriate technologies.
This thin, protective tissue type lines the outer surfaces of organs and the inner surfaces of blood vessels; the skin's outermost layer is a familiar example. What is it?
Epithelium is a thin, continuous, protective layer of cells with little extracellular matrix.

Discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb in 1952 and named for a pioneer of nuclear physics, element 100 is the heaviest that neutron bombardment can produce. Which synthetic element is it?
Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
The largest living primate, with arm spans reaching 2.6 metres, this equatorial-African great ape shares up to 99% of its DNA with humans — what is it?
Gorilla are large, primarily herbivorous, great apes that live in the tropical forests of equatorial Africa.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.
Founder of Romania's Social Democratic Party, this engineer served two separate stints as president after playing a leading role in the 1989 revolution that toppled Ceaușescu — who is he?

Ion Iliescu (3 March 1930 - 5 August 2025) was a Romanian politician and engineer who served as the first and third President of Romania since the country's transition to democracy, from 1990 to 1996 and 2000 to 2004.
The youngest division chief in GM history, this engineer shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the company behind a famously gull-winged car — who was he?
John DeLorean (d-; January 6, 1925 - March 19, 2005) was an American engineer, inventor, and executive in the U.S.
This unit of speed equals exactly one nautical mile per hour, roughly 1.15 mph, and is the standard measure used in maritime and aviation contexts — what is it called?
Knot (unit) is a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, exactly 1.852 km/h (approximately 1.151 mph or 0.514 m/s).

Equal to about 9.46 trillion kilometres, this astronomical distance unit is defined by how far illumination travels through a vacuum in 365.25 days — despite its name, it isn't a measure of time. What is it?
Light-year (ly or lyr), is a unit of length used to express astronomical distances and is equal to exactly 9460730472580.8 km, which is approximately 9.46 trillion kilometres or 5.88 trillion miles.
Which Australian nut-producing tree genus, an important bushfood for Aboriginal peoples, was first commercially cultivated at scale not in its native country but in Hawaii?
Macadamia is a genus of four species of trees in the flowering plant family Proteaceae.

These aquatic insects carry ancient traits from the first flying insects — long tails and wings that won't fold flat — and their water-dwelling young are a living signal of clean, unpolluted streams; what bug is this?
Mayfly (also up-winged flies or up-wing flies, or drake-flies in the UK; shadflies or fishflies in northern U.S.
Widowed in 2021, this Israeli-American billionaire physician publishes Israel Hayom and has been among the most prominent financial supporters of a US president since 2016 — who is she?
Miriam Adelson (ne Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
This protective plate at fingertips and toe-tips is found in nearly every primate except marmosets, and is made of the same tough protein found in claws, hooves, and horns — what is it?

Nail (anatomy) is a protective plate characteristically found at the tip of the digits (fingers and toes) of almost all primates (except for marmosets), corresponding to the claws in other tetrapod animals.
The smallest of its type, this Canadian gun dog has webbed feet and lures waterfowl to shore with playful antics before fetching them from the water — which breed is it?
Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever is a medium-sized gun dog bred primarily for hunting.

Created by Danish-Canadian programmer Rasmus Lerdorf in 1993 and released in 1995, this general-purpose scripting language was originally short for 'Personal Home Page' before becoming a recursive backronym — name the language?
PHP is a general-purpose scripting language geared towards web development.
Named from Greek words for 'odd' and 'toe,' this mammalian order groups horses, rhinoceroses, and tapirs together based on their toe count. Which order?
Perissodactyla (from Ancient Greek, perisss 'odd' and, dktylos 'finger, toe'), or odd-toed ungulates, is an order of ungulates.
A member of the cashew family and a priority tree-nut allergen, this green seed saw the US, Iran, and Turkey produce 87% of the world's 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — what is it?
Pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
Split into the strepsirrhines — lemurs and lorisids — and the haplorhines — tarsiers, monkeys and apes — this order ranges in size down to tiny Madame Berthe's — what is it?

Primate is an order of mammals, which is further divided into the strepsirrhines, which include lemurs, galagos, and lorisids; and the haplorhines, which include tarsiers and simians (monkeys and apes).

Founding an organization promoting swadeshi economics against globalization, this Indian social activist later allied with a yoga guru to combine that economic message with the promotion of yoga and Ayurveda — who is he?
Rajiv Dixit (30 November 1967 - 30 November 2010) was an Indian social activist who founded the Azadi Bachao Andolan.

This long-term skin condition causes facial redness, pimples, and swelling, and can lead to a severely enlarged, reddened nose in extreme cases — its exact cause remains unknown — name this condition?
Rosacea is a long-term skin condition that typically affects the face.

These pinnipeds, distinguished from true seals by their external ear flaps and ability to walk on all fours, belong to the eared-seal family alongside fur seals, with six living species worldwide. What animal is this?
Sea lion are pinnipeds characterized by external ear flaps, long foreflippers, the ability to walk on all fours, short and thick hair, and a big chest and belly.
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings (designated A, B, C, and D) arranged in a specific molecular configuration.

Restricted today to Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines, these tree-dwelling primates make up the only living family in their taxonomic order and thrive in liana-rich forests — which animal?
Tarsier are haplorhine primates of the family Tarsiidae, which is the lone extant family within the infraorder Tarsiiformes.

Affecting roughly 10 to 15 percent of people, this condition causes a person to hear ringing or other sounds with no external source, and its name comes from the Latin word for 'to ring' — what is it?
Tinnitus is a condition when a person hears a ringing sound or a different variety of sounds when no corresponding external sound is present and that other people cannot hear.
Medically called micturition or voiding, this voluntary process happens up to seven times a day in a healthy adult — and goes by "number one." What is it?
Urination is the release of urine from the bladder through the urethra in placental mammals, or through the cloaca in other vertebrates.

First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass genus is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop, with varieties including spelt, durum, and einkorn — name the crop?
Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
A branch of morphology with roots in prehistoric times, which natural science studies the internal and external structure of organisms and their parts?
Anatomy: Study of the structure of organisms. Anatomy is a branch of natural science that deals with the structural organization of living things.
Most often caused by stroke or head trauma, this condition impairs a person's ability to understand or produce language because specific brain regions aren't working. What is it?
Aphasia: Inability to comprehend or formulate language.

With the symbol At and atomic number 85, this is the rarest naturally occurring element in Earth's crust, so radioactive that a macroscopic sample would instantly vaporize itself — what element is it?
Astatine: Chemical element with atomic number 85 (At). It is the rarest naturally occurring element in the Earth's crust, occurring only as the decay product of various heavier elements.

The most widespread bird in its family, found on every continent except Antarctica (where only stray vagrants appear), this species has blue upperparts, a deeply forked tail, and usually nests in man-made structures — what is it?
Barn swallow: Species of bird. The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.
Before becoming TV's most famous bow-tied science educator, this Boeing mechanical engineer invented a hydraulic resonance suppressor tube for 747s, then quit to do sketch comedy. Who is he?
Modified from a 747-200B and nicknamed the 'Doomsday plane,' this USAF aircraft serves as a survivable airborne command post for the president during nuclear war — which aircraft?
Boeing E-4: US Air Force airborne command squadron aircraft.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and spread mainly through infected fleas, this illness produces swollen, painful lymph nodes nicknamed 'buboes' — what disease?
Bubonic plague: Human and animal disease.
This biological family includes wolves, foxes, jackals, and domestic dogs, ranging in size from the 6.6-foot gray wolf down to the tiny fennec fox — what is it called?
Canidae: Family of mammals. Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine, this class of molecules includes adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine, and drives the fight-or-flight response when released from the adrenal glands. What are they called?
Caused by a member of the herpesvirus family, this airborne illness usually starts on the chest, back, and face before the itchy little blisters scab over all over the body — what is it?
Its visible portion, the glans, is roughly the size of a pea yet packs over 10,000 nerve endings, making it the primary source of female sexual pleasure. What is this organ?
Clitoris: Erectile female sexual organ. In amniotes, the clitoris (KLIT-ər-iss or klih-TOR-iss; pl.: clitorises or clitorides) is a female sex organ.

This small, ground-nesting game bird has a call of three quick chirps repeated in succession, breeds across Europe, and winters in Africa and southern India — which species, often confused with a similar-sounding Japanese cousin?
Common quail: Species of bird. The common quail (Coturnix coturnix) or European quail is a small ground-nesting game bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae.

Ancient Greek, Chinese, and Indian cultures lacked a concept for this, seeing art as discovery rather than invention, while the Judeo-Christian-Islamic tradition later reserved it for God alone — what mental faculty is this?
Creativity: Forming something new and somehow valuable.
Also known as jimsonweed or devil's trumpet, this poisonous nightshade plant likely native to Central America has been used both in folk medicine and, unpleasantly, as a hallucinogen — which plant?
Datura stramonium: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Nicknamed the 'businessman's trip' in the 1960s for its rapid onset and short duration, which naturally occurring tryptamine hallucinogen has long been used as a ritual entheogen?
Of the 68 species bearing this name, only the Aquilinae are genetically "true" ones — the rest just qualify as any bird of prey big enough to hunt sizeable vertebrates; what's the common name?
Eagle: Large bird of prey. Eagle is the common name for certain large birds of prey within the family of the Accipitridae.
This messenger network of hormone feedback loops releases chemicals from internal glands like the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal glands straight into the bloodstream to regulate distant organs?
Endocrine system: Hormone-producing glands of a body.

A women's-rights campaigner schooled in 1830s New York, she was the first scientist to show certain gases trap heat — anticipating that rising CO2 could warm the climate. Who was this overlooked pioneer?
Eunice Newton Foote: American scientist and activist (1819–1888)
Carnivora splits into two suborders, dog-like and cat-like — which one groups cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids together?

Passed down through generations rather than taught in a classroom, this field covers oral traditions like legends and proverbs as well as customs like festivals and traditional building styles — what is it called?
Folklore: Expressive culture shared by particular groups.
Sometimes called 'poor man's pepper' or 'pepper grass,' this fast-growing herb has a peppery bite similar to mustard — which plant?
Garden cress: Species of edible herb.

Inducted into the U.S. Air Force Hall of Fame in 2018, this American mathematician modeled the precise shape of the Earth — work later baked into the Global Positioning System that now guides your phone. Who is she?
Rising from the ashes of the cancelled F-111B, which variable-sweep-wing Navy fighter first flew in 1970 and deployed aboard USS Enterprise?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat: Carrier-based multi-role fighter aircraft family.
Spiny like a porcupine but actually a distant cousin of the shrew, this nocturnal little mammal comes in 17 species across Europe, Asia, and Africa — and was introduced to New Zealand; what is it?

Widely credited as the 'father of the Indian nuclear programme,' this theoretical physicist founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and chaired India's first Atomic Energy Commission — who is it?
Homi J. Bhabha: Indian nuclear physicist (1909–1966)

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
Also called the red date or Chinese date, this buckthorn-family fruit is eaten fresh, dried, or candied — what is it?
Jujube: Species of plant with edible fruit.
Named from a Norwegian word for 'small fry of fish,' these shrimp-like crustaceans form a biomass of some 379 million tonnes in the Southern Ocean alone — which creatures?

Krill: Small, shrimp-like crustaceans; order of crustaceans. Krill (Euphausiids) (sing.: krill) are small and exclusively marine crustaceans of the order Euphausiacea, found in all of the world's oceans.
Together with pikas, this mammal family — comprising rabbits and hares — makes up the order Lagomorpha and includes over 70 species — which family?
Leporidae: Family of lagomorphs. Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Best known in its heptahydrate form as Epsom salt, this white crystalline compound (MgSO4) is also used in agriculture to fix soils deficient in an essential plant nutrient — what compound is it?
Magnesium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula MgSO4.
Awarded a share of the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physics for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, this Göttingen-trained theorist helped found quantum mechanics — who is he?
First isolated in 1921 and encoded by the codon AUG, this essential amino acid also serves as the precursor to cysteine — which amino acid is this?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.
Considered a cultural universal present in every human society, this medium arranges sound into harmony, melody, and rhythm through composition, improvisation, and performance — what is it?
Music: Form of art using sound.

First arising in wormlike organisms 550 to 600 million years ago, this body-wide network splits into a central hub of brain and spinal cord and a peripheral web of nerve fibers relaying signals to and from every body part — which network?
Nervous system: Part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses.
Practitioners of this field are sometimes mistaken for mere coin collectors, but they study all means of paying debts — even the horses the Kyrgyz once used as currency. What's the field called?
Numismatics: Study of currencies, coins and paper money.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.

Native to southern Brazil, Paraguay and northern Argentina, this vine produces a round berry that turns yellow or dark purple at maturity, prized for its juicy, seed-filled interior — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Passiflora edulis: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
Known online by the alias 'brokep,' this Swedish-born entrepreneur co-founded a famous BitTorrent search engine before launching the privacy-focused registrar Njalla in 2017 — who is he?
Peter Sunde: Swedish entrepreneur and politician. Peter Sunde Kolmisoppi (born 13 September 1978), alias brokep, is a Swedish-born Finnish-Norwegian entrepreneur and politician.
Known as the Scots pine in Britain, this Eurasian conifer is identifiable by its blue-green needles and orange-red bark — which species?
Pinus sylvestris: Species of conifer. Pinus sylvestris is a species of tree in the pine family Pinaceae that is native to Eurasia.
Also known as niter or saltpeter, this compound is a key ingredient of traditional gunpowder and gives cured meats their reddish color — what is it?
Potassium nitrate: Chemical compound. Potassium nitrate is a chemical compound with a sharp, salty, bitter taste and the chemical formula KNO3.
Fossils of this genus, found in Germany's Solnhofen limestone, mark the first pterosaur ever identified as a flying reptile — which genus?
Pterodactylus: Genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Late Jurassic.
This genus of muroid rodents gives its scientific name to the common rat, though not every animal called a rat actually belongs to it — which genus?
Sold under the brand name Rituxan, this monoclonal antibody treats non-Hodgkin lymphoma, rheumatoid arthritis and several other autoimmune conditions via slow IV infusion — what is it?
Named after a 19th-century American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, flagella-covered bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes divided among just two species — what is it?
Salmonella: Genus of bacteria. Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
This class of central nervous system depressant increases GABA activity to calm irritability and anxiety, distinct from drugs used mainly to induce sleep — what is it?
Sedative: Drug that reduces excitement without inducing sleep.
In this rare congenital condition affecting about 1 in 10,000 people, the heart and other major organs sit as a mirror image of their normal position — what's it called?
Situs inversus: Condition in which organs are reversed.

Made of a segmented series of bones cushioned by intervertebral discs, this defining feature of some 50,000 animal species surrounds and protects the nerve tissue running through it — what is it, also known as the backbone?
Spinal column: Bony structure found in vertebrates.
Signified by the minus sign, this arithmetic operation represents removing objects from a collection and is the inverse of addition — which operation is it?
Subtraction: One of the four basic arithmetic operations.
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
